subject: astronomy
title: Celestial Sphere Foundations
welcome_lead: Map the sky like an astronomer using the celestial sphere.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy: celestial sphere, equator, ecliptic and key reference points.
final_note: You now have the vocabulary to describe positions on the sky.

concepts.def: Imaginary sphere around Earth with stars fixed on it.
Projection of Earth's equator onto celestial sphere.
Sun's apparent path through the sky over one year.
Point on celestial sphere directly above observer.
Point directly below observer, opposite the zenith.
Star that never sets, always above horizon.

walkthroughs.body_html: Stars are so far away they look fixed on an imaginary sphere around Earth. The Earth's axis projects onto this sphere giving the celestial poles, with Polaris very close to the north celestial pole.
The celestial equator is the projection of Earth's equator. The ecliptic is the Sun's annual path, tilted ~23.5 degrees because Earth's axis is tilted.
Stars within an angle equal to your latitude from the celestial pole never set. From the UK (~52 N), Polaris and stars in Ursa Major are circumpolar.
